The question is how to own your [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-5|The Full]].

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Gumroad payhip

Gumroad and Payhip are rental platforms. They offer hosting, payment processing, and product delivery—all tied to their infrastructure. You pay a percentage of every sale. Sovereign commerce stacks are owned infrastructure. You deploy GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for crypto transactions. No subscriptions. No platform lock-in. The tradeoff: You configure the stack once. The reward: You own it forever. Gumroad and Payhip are simpler to start but riskier to scale. Sovereign stacks require initial setup but deliver permanent control.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Gumroad and Payhip fail in restricted countries because Stripe and PayPal fail. If Stripe doesn’t operate in your country, Gumroad is useless. If PayPal suspends your account, Payhip freezes your revenue. Sovereign stacks bypass these layers entirely. NOWPayments processes 300+ cryptocurrencies with a 0.5% fee—no KYC, no buyer account required. Transactions confirm on-chain. The webhook fires instantly. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON keep fees under $0.10. This is not a workaround. It’s base-layer infrastructure built for financial isolation.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Gumroad charges 10% per transaction. Payhip starts at 5%. Both add Stripe’s 2.9% + $0.30. In restricted countries, these fees are theoretical—you can’t use them. Sovereign stacks charge a flat 0.5% via NOWPayments. No platform fees. No hidden costs. Crypto payments settle in minutes, not days. The real cost is deployment time. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) deploys in 48 hours—Cloudflare Pages, Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments configured. Five products loaded. SPF/DKIM/DMARC set. End-to-end tested. This is not cheaper than Gumroad. It’s structurally different.
Stripe operates in 46 countries. Sovereign stacks operate in 195.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With Gumroad and Payhip, the platform owns your customer data, your product files, and your revenue stream. They can suspend your account at any time. Sovereign stacks give you full data ownership. Orders store in your Supabase database. Product files deliver from your Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Automation runs on your Cloudflare Workers. The customer owns everything after deployment. COREMERCH has no access. No platform dependency. No subscriptions. Lifetime access. This is infrastructure sovereignty—not renting, owning.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you’re in a Stripe-supported country and sell one product once, Gumroad or Payhip might suffice. If you’re in Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, or any restricted region, these platforms are non-starters. Sovereign commerce stacks are the only structural alternative. They require initial setup but deliver permanent control. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is deployed in 48 hours—ready to sell. The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) provides full documentation if you deploy yourself. Choose rental platforms if you accept platform risk. Choose sovereign infrastructure if you demand ownership.
